P004-D001.title: Discharge letter after pacemaker implantation
P004-D001.text:
Dear colleagues,
We report on the stay of Mr Rudolf Hofer, born 30.08.1941, from 15.03.2019 to 18.03.2019.

Reason for admission: high-grade second-degree AV block, Mobitz type, symptomatic bradycardia (HR 34/min), syncope.
Previous illnesses: chronic heart failure (HFrEF, EF about 38% in 2018), ischaemic cardiomyopathy (inferior myocardial infarction 2003), arterial hypertension, CKD stage 3 (creatinine about 1.8 mg/dl), dementia (mild, MMSE 22/30, 2018).

Implant: dual-chamber pacemaker (DDD), Medtronic Advisa DR MRI SureScan, generator left subclavian, leads RA + RV. X-ray after surgery: both leads correctly placed.

Allergies: according to the patient and his daughter: no known allergies.
Medication at discharge (2019): ramipril 5 mg 1-0-0, bisoprolol 5 mg 1-0-0, furosemide 40 mg 1-0-0, spironolactone 25 mg 1-0-0, aspirin 100 mg 1-0-0, atorvastatin 40 mg 0-0-1, pantoprazole 40 mg 1-0-0.

Recommendation: pacemaker check every 6–12 months. Continue heart failure therapy.
Kind regards, Senior Dr Gerhard Moser, cardiology, Klinikum Linz-Nord

P004-D002.title: Dementia check: moderate Alzheimer's dementia
P004-D002.text:
Patient Rudolf Hofer, born 30.08.1941, male. Check at the memory clinic.
Accompanied by his daughter Ingrid Hofer.

Cognition: MMSE 16/30 (worse than 2021: 19/30). Clock test: severely impaired. Clearly disoriented to time and place. Self-care: increasingly dependent on help.
Diagnosis: Alzheimer's dementia (G30.1), moderate (ICD F00.1). Rivastigmine patch 9.5 mg/24 h already well tolerated.

Previous illnesses: chronic heart failure, CKD 3b, arterial hypertension, pacemaker 2019.
Family history: daughter with genetically confirmed dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM, LMNA mutation) – not related to the patient's illness.

Medication (according to daughter, 10/2023): ramipril 5 mg, bisoprolol 5 mg, furosemide 40 mg, spironolactone 25 mg, aspirin 100 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, pantoprazole 40 mg, rivastigmine patch 9.5 mg/24 h, donepezil 5 mg 0-0-1 (since 09/2022).
Allergies: none known.

P004-D004.title: Admission report, internal medicine
P004-D004.text:
Admission: 04.11.2024, 11:30, ward IM-4
Patient: Hofer Rudolf, born 30.08.1941, male

Referral diagnosis: decompensated heart failure.

History: because of dementia the patient cannot give an adequate history. From his daughter: increasing shortness of breath for 5 days, orthopnoea, leg swelling, weight gain +4 kg.

Previous illnesses:
- Chronic heart failure (HFrEF)
- Ischaemic cardiomyopathy, inferior myocardial infarction 2003
- Arterial hypertension
- CKD stage 3b
- Alzheimer's dementia (moderate)
- Pacemaker implantation (DDD, 2019)
No known allergies.
Smoking: ex-smoker since 1985.

Physical examination:
General condition reduced, short of breath at rest. Weight 78 kg (daughter: usually about 74 kg), height 171 cm.
Heart: paced regular rhythm, systolic murmur 2/6 at the apex. Pulse 68/min (pacemaker rate).
Lungs: moist crackles at both bases. Dull percussion at both bases.
Limbs: swelling of both legs up to the knees, lower legs tense with oedema.
Abdomen: soft, liver 2 finger-breadths below the costal margin.
Neuro: awake, disoriented to time and place, limited cooperation.
BP 168/94 mmHg. SpO2 91% on room air.

ECG: paced rhythm 68/min, pacing spikes visible, LBBB pattern (pacemaker-induced), no acute ischaemia.

Diagnosis (provisional): decompensated chronic heart failure (I50.0).

Plan:
- Lab STAT incl. BNP, troponin, kidney values
- Chest X-ray
- Furosemide 80 mg IV now
- Oxygen 2 l/min
- Daily weight
- Pacemaker check
- Continue all home medication for now

P004-D005.title: Nursing report, day of admission
P004-D005.text:
04.11.2024, 12:30, registered nurse Rosa Gruber

Patient Hofer Rudolf, IM-4, bed 3. Admitted with his daughter. Disoriented, cooperates with guidance.
Daughter Ingrid Hofer reports: the patient once reacted to a sulfonamide antibiotic (she thinks "co-trimoxazole") – rash. That was very long ago (about 20 years). She is unsure whether it was co-trimoxazole or something else.
Passed on to the ward doctor.
No urinary incontinence. Bowels opened yesterday.
Oxygen 2 l/min running, SpO2 now 93%. Urine output after IV furosemide: 800 ml in 2 h.
Positioning: upper body raised 30–45°. Pressure ulcer prevention activated (Braden score 14).
Medication: rivastigmine patch changed (new site). Donepezil planned for the evening.
When asked, the patient says he "had heart surgery" in the past. Daughter confirms: only the pacemaker, no open heart surgery.

P004-D007.title: Chest X-ray in heart failure
P004-D007.text:
Report: chest X-ray AP, 04.11.2024
Patient: Hofer Rudolf, born 30.08.1941

Clinical question: decompensated heart failure.

Findings:
Heart: clearly enlarged (cardiomegaly), cardiothoracic ratio >0.6.
Pacemaker generator left subclavian with two leads (RA and RV), correctly placed.
Lungs: opacities at both bases, consistent with pleural effusions. Peribronchial cuffing. Increased vascular markings (pulmonary congestion).
No pneumothorax. No infiltrates suggesting pneumonia.

Assessment:
1. Clear signs of pulmonary congestion with pleural effusions on both sides in decompensated heart failure.
2. Pacemaker generator with two leads in correct position.
3. No sign of pneumonia.

P004-D008.title: Progress note day 1 – good diuresis, spironolactone paused for potassium
P004-D008.text:
05.11.2024, 08:00, Dr Daniela Fuchs
Day 1 after admission.

Patient slightly better. SpO2 94% on 2 l O2. Shortness of breath slightly decreasing. Oedema: minimally better.
Urine output yesterday: 2,400 ml in total (after furosemide 80 mg IV).
Weight today: 76.5 kg (yesterday 78 kg → -1.5 kg).
BP 158/88, pulse 68/min (paced).

Lab call-back: K+ 5.2 mmol/l → spironolactone paused (risk of hyperkalaemia with CKD + ramipril).
Ramipril temporarily reduced to 2.5 mg (kidney values + hyperkalaemia).

Cardiology consult requested.

Nursing report (daughter): suspected sulfonamide allergy documented, still unclear whether clinically relevant → to be discussed in the consult.

Pneumonia?: chest X-ray yesterday – no infiltrates, no sign. CRP 18 mg/l could be raised by congestion in heart failure. Suspected pneumonia currently not maintained.

Plan:
- Continue furosemide 80 mg IV
- Spironolactone PAUSED
- Ramipril 2.5 mg (reduced)
- Lab tomorrow

P004-D009.title: Sulfonamide allergy check – discussion
P004-D009.text:
05.11.2024, 09:30, Dr Fuchs

Discussed with the senior doctor because of the reported sulfonamide allergy (daughter reports a possible co-trimoxazole reaction about 20 years ago).
Senior doctor decision: record the allergy as unconfirmed but plausible. Note co-trimoxazole in the patient file as a caution.
Clinical relevance for current treatment: low (no sulfonamide planned). No further testing (patient cannot be tested because of dementia, daughter unsure).

Entry in the allergy profile: sulfonamides (co-trimoxazole) – suspected drug rash, unconfirmed, reported by a relative.

P004-D010.title: Cardiology consultation – decompensated HFrEF
P004-D010.text:
Cardiology consultation report, 06.11.2024
Consultant: Senior Dr Petra Mayr, cardiology

Reason: decompensated HFrEF, medication review, echo.

Echocardiography (06.11.2024):
- LV: EF 35% (clearly reduced), diffuse hypokinesia (ischaemic cardiomyopathy)
- Mitral regurgitation: 2/4, functional
- No pericardial effusion
- Right heart: RV moderately dilated, estimated PA pressure 42 mmHg
- Pacemaker leads: correctly placed RA + RV

Note: the admission report (D004) did not document the EF; when asked, the resident mentioned "EF 30%". The echo correctly shows **EF 35%**. The echo report is authoritative.

Recommendations:
1. Reduce furosemide from 80 mg IV to 40 mg orally 1-0-0 when oedema decreases (target dry weight 74 kg).
2. Keep spironolactone paused (K+ >5). Check K+ daily.
3. When K+ is normal: eplerenone 25 mg 1-0-0 as an alternative (less gynaecomastia, somewhat better tolerated in CKD).
4. Ramipril: 2.5 mg for now, increase back to 5 mg once kidney values are stable.
5. Continue bisoprolol 5 mg.
6. Heart failure teaching for the daughter (weight monitoring, fluids).
7. Pacemaker check by the pacemaker clinic.

P004-D011.text:

P004-D012.title: Progress note day 5 – switch to oral diuretic, eplerenone
P004-D012.text:
09.11.2024, 08:00, Senior Dr Markus Berger

Patient clinically much better. SpO2 96% on room air. Orthopnoea gone. Oedema: clearly decreasing.
Weight today: 74.8 kg (admission 78 kg → -3.2 kg).

Lab yesterday (08.11.):
  K+: 4.5 mmol/l – normal again.
  Creatinine: 1.82 mg/dl, eGFR 35.

Furosemide switched: 80 mg IV → furosemide 40 mg orally 1-0-0 (per cardiology consult).
Eplerenone 25 mg 1-0-0 started (K+ now normal, per cardiology recommendation).
Ramipril: back to 5 mg (kidney values stable).

Spironolactone stays stopped (hyperkalaemia occurred on spironolactone + ramipril + CKD; eplerenone as the alternative).

Donepezil: continue (dementia treatment).
Rivastigmine patch: continue.

Plan:
- Continue weight monitoring
- Pacemaker clinic appointment booked: 12.11.
- Discharge 14–15.11. at the earliest

Mr Hofer, discharge planned tomorrow. Good general condition, no shortness of breath, SpO2 97% on room air.

P004-D016.title: Discharge letter after decompensated heart failure
P004-D016.text:
Discharge letter
Musterstadt Regional Hospital, Internal Medicine
Date: 15.11.2024

Dear Dr Weiss,

We are discharging Mr Rudolf Hofer, born 30.08.1941, after an inpatient stay from 04.11.2024 to 15.11.2024 (11 days).

Main diagnoses:
1. Decompensated chronic heart failure (HFrEF, EF 35%) (I50.0)
2. Ischaemic cardiomyopathy, inferior myocardial infarction 2003 (I25.2)
3. Chronic kidney disease stage 3b (eGFR 36 ml/min) (N18.3)
4. Alzheimer's dementia, moderate (F00.1)
5. Arterial hypertension (I10)
6. Hyperkalaemia on spironolactone (E87.5) – improved after the switch

Course:
Admitted with decompensated heart failure (BNP 2,480, oedema, orthopnoea). Weight gain +4 kg. Furosemide 80 mg IV → good diuresis. Spironolactone paused because of hyperkalaemia (K+ 5.2). After K+ normalised, eplerenone 25 mg started as the alternative. Ramipril reduced to 2.5 mg, back to 5 mg once kidney values were stable. Pacemaker check: normal (battery 78%, about 4 years remaining).

Allergies: CAUTION sulfonamides (co-trimoxazole) – suspected drug rash, reported by his daughter, unconfirmed (patient cannot give information).
Note: no open heart surgery in the history (only pacemaker implantation 2019). The patient repeatedly reports "heart surgery" – this refers to the pacemaker.

Medication at discharge:
1. Ramipril 5 mg (Delix) 1-0-0
2. Bisoprolol 5 mg (Concor) 1-0-0
3. Furosemide 40 mg (Lasix) 1-0-0
4. Eplerenone 25 mg (Inspra) 1-0-0 (NEW – replaces spironolactone)
5. Aspirin 100 mg 1-0-0
6. Atorvastatin 40 mg 0-0-1
7. Pantoprazole 40 mg 1-0-0
8. Rivastigmine patch 9.5 mg/24 h (Exelon)
9. Donepezil 5 mg (Aricept) 0-0-1

Implant: dual-chamber pacemaker DDD (Medtronic Advisa DR MRI SureScan), implanted 15.03.2019, Klinikum Linz-Nord.

Recommendations:
- Daily weight; if weight gain >2 kg/day → see the GP immediately
- Lab (K+, creatinine) in 1 week
- Pacemaker clinic check in 12 months
- Dementia: memory clinic check as planned

Please continue treatment.
Kind regards, Senior Dr Markus Berger, internal medicine
Musterstadt Regional Hospital
